questions.q: One mole of $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{H}_4$ loses 10 moles of electrons to form a new compound $Z$. Assuming that all the nitrogens appear in the new compound, what is the oxidation state of nitrogen in $Z$ ? (There is no change in the oxidation state of hydrogen.)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{H}_4-10 e^{-} \longrightarrow X^{10+}$ (with two $\mathrm{N}$ atoms)
Total oxidation number of two $\mathrm{N}$ atoms in $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{H}_4$,
$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad 2 x+4 & =0 \\ 2 x & =-4\end{aligned}\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{H}_4$ loses 10 electrons, so total oxidation number of two $\mathrm{N}$-atoms increases by 10 , i.e., the total oxidation number of two $\mathrm{N}$-atoms in
$Y=-4+10=+6\therefore$ Oxidation number of each $\mathrm{N}$ atom in
$X^{10+}=+3$

questions.q:
From the given reactions identify the disproportionation reaction
i) ${Cl}_{2} ( g ) + 2KI ( aq ) ⟶ 2KCl ( aq ) + {I}_{2} ( s )$
ii) ${Cl}_{2} ( g ) + 2{OH}^{-} ( aq ) ⟶ {ClO}^{-} ( aq ) + {Cl}^{-} ( aq ) + {H}_{2}O ( l )$
iii) $Mg ( s ) + 2HCl ( aq ) ⟶ {MgCl}_{2} ( aq ) + {H}_{2} ( g )$
iv) $2{H}_{2}{O}_{2} ( aq ) ⟶ 2{H}_{2}O ( l ) + {O}_{2} ( g )$
questions.solution:
The reaction in which one reactant gets oxidized, and the same reactant gets reduced is known as disproportionation reaction.&

$\overset{0}{Cl}2 ( g ) + 2K\overset{- 1}{I} ( aq ) ⟶ 2K\overset{0}{C}l ( aq ) + \overset{- 1}{I}2 ( s )$

In the above reaction different elements undergoing oxidation and reduction. Hence, It is not a~disproportionation reaction.~

$\overset{0}{Cl}2 ( g ) + 2{OH}^{-} ( aq ) ⟶ \overset{+ 1}{Cl}O^{-} ( aq ) + {Cl}^{-} ( aq ) + {H}_{2}O ( l )$

In the above reaction chlorine is undergoing oxidation as well as reduction.~Hence, It is a disproportionation reaction.~

$\overset{0}{Mg} ( s ) + 2\overset{+ 1}{H}Cl ( aq ) ⟶ \overset{+ 2}{Mg}{Cl}_{2} ( aq ) + \overset{0}{H}2 ( g )$

In the above reaction magnesium is undergoing oxidation and hydrogen ion undergoing reduction.~Hence, It is not a~disproportionation reaction.~

$2{H}_{2}\overset{- 1}{O}2 ( aq ) ⟶ 2{H}_{2}\overset{- 2}{O} ( l ) + \overset{0}{O}2 ( g )$

In the above reaction peroxide is undergoing oxidation as well as reduction.& Hence, It is a disproportionation reaction.&
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: During a redox titration involving a solution containing ${Fe}^{2 +}$ ions against $Mn{O}_{4}^{-}$ in the presence of excess of $H^{+}$ ions, the number of electrons that gets transferred is
questions.solution:
For redox titration of a solution containing& ${Fe}^{2 +}$~against~${MnO}_{4}^{-}$,~$H^{+}$~ions are present in excess i.e., the solution~is acidic.

$\overset{+ 7}{Mn}{O}_{4}^{-} + {Fe}^{2 +} \to {Fe}^{3 +} + {Mn}^{2 +} ( acidicmedium )$

Here, oxidation number of~$Mn$~is reduced from~$+ 7to + 2$~(reduction)~and oxidation number of~$Fe$~is increased from~$+ 2to + 3$(oxidation).

Reduction half cell,

${MnO}_{4}^{-} + 8H^{+} + 5e^{-} ⟶ {Mn}^{2 +} + 4{H}_{2}O$....(equation 1)

Oxidation half cell,

[$Fe^{2 +} ⟶ Fe^{3 +} + e^{-} ] \times 5$.....(equation 2)

By adding equation 1 and 2, final balanced reaction will be,

${MnO}_{4}^{-} + 8H^{+} + 5{Fe}^{2 +} ⟶ {Mn}^{2 +} + 5{Fe}^{3 +} + 4{H}_{2}O$
Therefore, five electrons gets transferred.
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: \(20 $\mathrm{~mL}$\) of \$(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$\) solution of certain concentration has completely reacted with \(20 $\mathrm{~mL}$\) of \(0.01 $\mathrm{M} \mathrm{K}}_{2} $\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}\) in acidic medium. If \(20 $\mathrm{~mL}$\) of same \$(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$\) solution has reacted completely with \(20 $\mathrm{~mL}$\) of \$(\mathrm{KMnO}}_{4}\) solution in acid medium, the molarity of \$(\mathrm{KMnO}}_{4}\) solution is$
questions.solution: The reaction between \$(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$\) and \$(\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}^{2-}\) (i.e. \$(\mathrm{K}}_{2} $\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}\)) in acidic medium occurs as follows : \$(\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}^{2-}+14 \mathrmH^{+}+6 $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} \longrightarrow$2 $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+$7 $\mathrm{H}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}+$6 $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$\) The reaction between \$(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$\) and \$(\mathrm{MnO}}_{4}^{-}\) (i.e. \$(\mathrm{KMnO}}_{4}\)) in acidic medium occurs as follows : \$(\mathrm{MnO}}_{4}^{-}+8 \mathrmH^{+}+5 $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}+$4 $\mathrm{H}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}+$5 $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$\) \(\therefore $\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}^{2-}\) react with \(6 $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$n_1\) and \$(\mathrm{MnO}}_{4}^{-}\)react with \(5 $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\left($n_2\right)\) in a balanced equation. Gram equivalent of \$(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$\) \(=\) gram equivalent of \$(\mathrm{K}}_{2} $\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}\) \(=\) gram equivalent of \$(\mathrm{KMnO}}_{4}\) Therefore, on comparing gram equivalent of \$(\mathrm{K}}_{2} $\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}\) and \$(\mathrm{KMnO}}_{4}\), we have \(n_1=6, n_2=5\) Conc. of \$(\mathrm{K}}_{2} $\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}=0.01 $\mathrm{M}\left($M_1\right)\) Volume of \$(\mathrm{K}}_{2} $\mathrm{Cr}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{7}=20 $\mathrm{~mL}\left($V_1\right)\) react with \$(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$\) ions \(=6 $\mathrm{~mol}\left($n_1\right)\) Conc. of \$(\mathrm{KMnO}}_{4}=\) to find (say \(M_2\)) Volume of \$(\mathrm{KMnO}}_{4}=20 $\mathrm{~mL}\left($V_2\right)\) react with \$(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$\) ions \(=5 $\mathrm{~mol}\left($n_2\right)\) Thus, \(\quad M_1 \times V_1 \times n_1=M_2 \times V_2 \times n_2\) or, \(0.01 \times 20 \times 6=M_2 \times 20 \times 5\) or \$(M_2=\frac{0.01 \times 6}{5}=$0.012 $\mathrm{M}$\) Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q: For the redox reaction& ${MnO}_{4}^{-} + {C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} + H^{+} \to {Mn}^{2 +} + {CO}_{2} + {H}_{2}O$, the correct coefficients of the reactants for the balanced reaction are respectively ${MnO}_{4}^{-}, {C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -}$ and $H^{+}$:
questions.solution:
For balancing the reaction four steps should be followed in the given order

& $1 .$~Balance elements i.e central metal which~oxidised or reduced.

~$2 .$~Balance oxygen by adding water molecules.

~$3 .$~Balance hydrogen by adding~$H^{+}$~ion.

~$4 .$~Balance charge by adding electrons.

Balancing~of reaction is given below:


$2{KMnO}_{4 } + 5{H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} + 3{H}_{2}{SO}_{4 } \to {K}_{2}{SO}_{4} + 2{MnSO}_{4} + 10{CO}_{2} + 8{H}_{2}O$
${MnO4}^{−} = - 2$
${C}_{2}{O4}^{- 2} = 5$
$H^{+} = 16$


Thus, the correct coefficients of~${MnO4}^{−}, {C}_{2}{O4}^{- 2}$ and~$H^{+}$~are~$2, 5\text{and}16$& respectively.

In the neutralization of acid and base $N \times V$ of both must be equivalent

$10 = 6 + 0 .25 V$

questions.q:
A student made the following observations in the laboratory.

I. Clean copper metal did not react with 1molar $Pb{\left(N{O}_{3}\right)}_{2}$ solution

II. Clean lead metal dissolved in a 1 molar $AgN{O}_{3}$ solution and crystals of $Ag$ metal appeared

III. Clean silver metal did not react with 1 molar $Cu{\left(N{O}_{3}\right)}_{2}$ solution

The order of decrease in reducing character of three metals is
questions.solution:
Metal placed above in electrochemical series replaces the other from its salt solution which is lower in the series.

The low $E^{o}$ value containing metals have the high reducing character.

Thus, order of reducing character of three metals is

$Pb > Cu > Ag$

A 10 mL portion of this solution required 14.5 mL of a normal HCl solution to reach the phenolphthalein end point. An another 10 mL portion of the same solution required 25 mL of the same HCl solution to reach the methyl orange end point. If the organic acid contains 26.23% oxygen by weight, deduce the strength of original NaOH solution.

Reaction of CO2 & NaOH

$2NaOH + C{O}_{2} ⟶ N{a}_{2}C{O}_{3} + {H}_{2}O$

Let 10 mL final solution has x mM Na2CO3~ and y mM of NaOH

y + x = 14.5~ (Phenolphthalein)

y + 2x = 25.0 ( Methyl orange)

Total mM of Na2CO3 Produced~ = $1 0 \text{.} 5 \times 1 0 0 = 1 0 5 0 \text{mM}$

= mM of CO2

$x = 10.5$

$y = 4$

$\mathop{2NaOH}_{2 \times 10.5} \text{+}\mathop{{\text{CO}}_{2}}_{10.5} \to N{a}_{2} C{O}_{3} {~+~H}_{2} O$

$∴ InitialNaOHin10ml = 21 + 4 = 25mmole$

$Normality = \dfrac{25}{10} = 2.5N$

questions.q:
Match the reactions given in column - I with the nature of the reaction/products given in column - II

$\begin{cases} & \text{Column - I} & & & \text{Column - II} \\ \left(\text{A}\right) & {MnO}_{4}^{2 -} \left(\text{aq}\right) + 4 H^{+} \left(\text{aq}\right) & ⟶ & \left(\text{p}\right) & \text{Show disproportionation} \\ \left(\text{B}\right) & {Cu}^{2 +} \left(\text{aq}\right) + I^{-} \left(\text{aq}\right) & ⟶ & \left(\text{q}\right) & \text{Redox reaction} \\ \left(\text{C}\right) & {CrO}_{4}^{2} \left(\text{aq}\right) + H^{+} \left(\text{aq}\right) & ⟶ & \left(\text{r}\right) & \text{One of the products is diamagnetic} \\ \left(\text{D}\right) & {Fe}^{3 +} \left(\text{aq}\right) + {\left[\text{Fe} {\left(\text{CN}\right)}_{6}\right]}^{4 -} \left(\text{aq}\right) & ⟶ & \left(\text{s}\right) & \text{One of the products has metal-oxygen-metal bond/linkage}\end{cases}$
questions.solution:
When oxidation and reduction take place on the same element of a compound is called a disproportionation reaction.&

The chemical reaction which involves transfer of electrons from one chemical substance to another is called a redox reaction.

A species which has no unpaired electron is called as diamagnetic.

(A)$\overset{\text{VI}}{Mn} {O}_{4}^{2 -} + 4 H^{+} ⟶ 2 \overset{\text{VII}}{Mn} {O}_{4}^{-} + \overset{\text{IV}}{Mn} {O}_{2} + 2 {H}_{2} \text{O}$

The oxidation state of~$Mn$~is changing from~$+ 6to + 7and + 6to + 4$. Hence it is a~disproportionation reaction, redox reaction and~${MnO}_{4}^{-}$~is diamagnetic in nature.

(B) $+ 2 - 1 + 1 - 102{Cu}^{2 +} + 4I^{-} \to {Cu}_{2}{I}_{2} ↓ + {I}_{2}$

It is a redox reaction and~${Cu}_{2}{I}_{2}$~is diamagnetic in nature.

(C) $2{CrO}_{4}^{2 -} + 2H^{+} \to {Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} + {H}_{2}\text{O}$

${Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -}$~is diamagnetic in nature and it also has~$Cr - O - Cr$~linkage.

(D) $4{Fe}^{3 +} + 3\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)6\right]4 - \to {Fe}_{4}\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)6\right]3$

${Fe}_{4}\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)6\right]3$& is diamangnetic in nature.

The first and second endpoints were found after adding $10mL$ and $15mL$ of $N / 10HCl$, respectively. The ratio of meq of ${Na}_{2}{CO}_{3}$ and ${NaHCO}_{3}$ in the solution is
questions.solution:
Let the meq of& ${Na}_{2}{CO}_{3}\text{and}{NaHCO}_{3}$ are~$a\text{and}b$, respectively.

Reactions taking place are as follows.

With phenolphthalein,

$HCl + {Na}_{2}{CO}_{3} \to {NaHCO}_{3} + NaCl$

This gives, meq of~$HCl = meqof{Na}_{2}{CO}_{3}$

$10 \times \dfrac{1}{10} = a \ldots \left(i\right)$

Later, with methyl orange,

$HCl + {NaHCO}_{3} \to {H}_{2}{CO}_{3} + NaCl$

This gives, meq of~$HCl = totalmeqof{NaHCO}_{3}$

$15 \times $\dfrac{1}{10} =$a + b \ldots \left(ii\right)$

On solving the two equations, we get,

$a = 1; b = 0 . 5\text{Required ratio of}meq = 2$

questions.q: Chlorine oxidises sulphur dioxide in the presence of water to give an oxyacid $A$. Chlorine also oxidises iodine in the presence of water to give an oxyacid $B$. The oxidation states of $\mathrm{S}$ and I in $A$ and $B$ are respectively
questions.solution: (i) When chlorine oxidises sulphur dioxide in presence of water, it gives $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ as oxyacid $(A)$. The reaction occurs as follows : \mathrm{Cl}_2+\mathrm{SO}_2+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4+2 \mathrm{HCl} The oxidation number of sulphur in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is 2+x+(4 x-2)=0 or, where $x=$ oxidation state of sulphur (S). x+2-8=0 \Rightarrow x=+6 Hence, oxidation state of (S) in $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is (+) 6 . (ii) When chlorine  \left(\mathrm{Cl}_2\right)$ oxidises iodine  \left(\mathrm{I}_2\right)$ in presence of water, it gives $\mathrm{HIO}_3$ as oxyacid $(B)$, the reaction occurs as follows: 5 \mathrm{Cl}_2+\mathrm{I}_2+6 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{HIO}_3+10 \mathrm{HCl} \text {. } The oxidation state of (I) in $\mathrm{HIO}_3$ is : Let oxidation state of $(\mathrm{I})=x\begin{aligned}$& 1+x+3 \times(-2)=0 \\ & x+1-6=0 \Rightarrow x=+5 \end{aligned} Hence, oxidation state of iodine (I) in $\mathrm{HIO}_3$ is $=(+) 5$ Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q: In which of the following transformations, oxygen is not the reducing agent?
questions.solution:
A reducing agent oxidises itself or liberates electrons for other reagents.
In the oxidation reaction, the& oxidation number increases.& In this reaction:& $4{NH}_{3} + 3{O}_{2} \to 2{N}_{2} + 6{H}_{2}O$~

The oxidation number~of oxygen in ${O}_{2}$~is zero and in ${H}_{2}O$~oxidation number of oxygen is $- 2$. Oxygen is reduced, so~${O}_{2}$~acts as an oxidising agent and does not act as reducing agent.

${Ag}_{2}O \to 2Ag + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2}$

In this~reaction, oxidation number of oxygen changes from $- 2$ to $0$. Here, oxidation takes place and~oxygen acts as a reducing agent.

$2{F}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O \to 4HF + {H}_{2}O$

In this reaction, the oxidation number~of oxygen remains same. So, oxygen is neither an oxidizing agent nor reducing agent.

${AgNO}_{3} + {H}_{2}{O}_{2} \to 2Ag + 2{HNO}_{3} + {O}_{2}$~

In this reaction, the oxidation number of oxygen changes from $- 1$ to $0$. It shows the oxidation of oxygen and here, oxygen acts as a reducing agent.

questions.q:
Why does the following reaction occur ?

${XeO}_{6}^{4 -}\left(\text{aq}\right) + 2F^{-}\left(\text{aq}\right) + 6H^{+}\left(\text{aq}\right) ⟶ {XeO}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right) + {F}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right) ++3{H}_{2}\text{O}\left(l ⁡\right)$

What conclusion about the compound ${Na}_{4}{XeO}_{6}$~ (of which ${XeO}_{6}^{4 -} is a part) can be drawn from the reaction ? select any one of the correct choice.$
options: $[ {XeO}_{6}{]}^{4 -}$ is a stronger oxidising agent than ${F}_{2}$
questions.solution:
Oxidation number change for the compounds in the reaction.

$\overset{+ 8}{Xe}{O}_{6}^{4 -}\left(aq ⁡\right) + 2\overset{- 1}{F{⁡}^{- 1}}\left(aq ⁡\right) + 6H^{+}\left(aq ⁡\right) ⟶ \overset{+ 6}{Xe}{O}_{3} \left(\text{g}\right) + \overset{0}{\text{F}2} ++3{H}_{2}\text{O}\left($l ⁡\right)$

In the above reaction:

  • Oxidation number of $Xe$ in ${XeO}_{6}^{4 -}$ decreases from $+ 8$ to $+ 6$ in ${XeO}_{3}$
  • Oxidation number of $F$ increases from $- 1$ (in $F^{-}$) to zero (in ${F}_{2}$).

Hence, ${XeO}_{6}^{4 -}$ or ${Na}_{4}{XeO}_{6}$ is reduced and $F^{-}$ is oxidised.

This reaction occurs because ${Na}_{4}{XeO}_{6}$ or ${XeO}_{6}^{4 -}$ is a stronger oxidising agent than fluorine.

$

questions.q: Which of the following reaction is a redox reaction ?
questions.solution:
Redox reaction is a reaction in which both oxidation and reduction occurs simentaneously.

  • Oxidation is gain in oxidation number
  • Reduction is loss in oxidation number.

1)& $\overset{+ 1}{Na}\overset{- 1}{Br} + \overset{+ 1}{H}\overset{- 1}{Cl} \to \overset{+ 1}{Na}\overset{- 1}{Cl} + \overset{+ 1}{H}\overset{- 1}{Br}$

there is no change in the oxidation numbers taking place, so no oxidation and no reduction in this reaction.

2)~$\overset{+ 1}{H}\overset{- 1}{Br} + \overset{+ 1}{Ag}\overset{+ 5}{N}\overset{- 2}{O}3 \to \overset{+ 1}{Ag}\overset{- 1}{Br} + \overset{+ 1}{H}\overset{+ 5}{N}\overset{- 2}{O}3$

there is no change in the oxidation numbers taking place, so no oxidation and no reduction in this reaction.

3)~$\overset{0}{H2} + \overset{0}{Br2} \to 2\overset{+ 1}{H}\overset{- 1}{Br}$

  • oxidation number of hydrogen is increasing hence oxidation is taking place.
  • oxidation number of bromine is decreasing hence reduction is taking place.

so the reaction is redox.

4)~$\overset{+ 1}{Na2}\overset{- 2}{O} + \overset{+ 1}{H2}\overset{+ 6}{S}\overset{- 2}{O4} \to \overset{+ 1}{Na2}\overset{+ 6}{S}\overset{- 2}{O4} + \overset{+ 1}{H2}\overset{- 2}{O}$

there is no change in the oxidation numbers taking place, so no oxidation and no reduction in this reaction.
